To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have obtained the one-loop folded string anomalous dimension in terms of integrable functions, and that we have used this result to derive the Konishi dimension and the finite-size effects for operators in the large S limit.
we have obtained the one-loop anomalous dimensions of short folded string states in the AdS/CFT correspondence and that our results are in agreement with the numerical data.
we have derived a general one-loop quantization formula for the folded string in AdS5×S5 and used it for the computation of anomalous dimensions of short operators in the large spin limit.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to the anomalous dimensions of the operators in N=4 SYM theory, based on the integrable string theory.
the study of the anomalous dimension for operators in N = 4 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory using the AdS/CFT correspondence.
a new approach to the anomalous dimensions of operators with small values of the R-charge.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our results for the folded string are in perfect agreement with all the available data.
the quantum folded string reproduces correctly all the known results for the Konishi anomalous dimension, and also for the anomalous dimensions of the states with small R-charge, at any coupling.
the folded string approach is able to reproduce correctly the strong coupling behavior of the short operators in the planar N = 4 super Yang-Mills theory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the folded string provides the correct answer to the Konishi dimension in the strong coupling regime.
the folded string solution is a very good candidate for the quantization of short operators in the gauge theory.
we have developed a powerful method which is able to compute the anomalous dimensions of operators with large Lorentz spin in the planar limit.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the algebraic curve is a powerful tool to obtain explicit results in integrable string theories.
the algebraic curve method can be applied to the folded string in AdS5 and that it is a powerful tool for computing finite-size effects and the anomalous dimensions of short operators.
the folded string solution can be used as an alternative to the BMN limit in the context of integrability.
